source.citation: National Register of Historic Places Inventory-Nomination Form, 'Prairie Avenue District', Chicago, Cook County, Illinois; prepared by John F. Hern, Commission on Chicago Historical and Architectural Landmarks, 17 March 1972.
what_it_does_not_supply: a Chicago School building on Prairie Avenue: the form names the style only as one Glessner House helped bring about, and as commercial architecture
any house's 1904 state: it describes the four houses as they stood in 1972
the granite's quarry beyond the form's own word 'Wellesley'
what_it_supplies: Glessner House as Romanesque, with rugged masonry, a round arch motif and a red-tiled gabled roof
that Glessner House is faced with heavily rusticated granite
the Kimball house as patterned on the Chateau de Josselin, and the Coleman house as a blend of the Glessner and Kimball styles
the Chicago School as a style of commercial architecture built on the steel frame, which the form says Glessner House helped to bring about
